title: Hold Periods and New-Seller Thresholds, Pocketwire Business Profile
content:
Hold periods on the Pocketwire Business Profile are counted in calendar days from the sale date. The new-seller figures are judged across all of the customer's business profiles. Column headings abbreviate the six tiers of the Pocketwire Business Profile: Pocketwire Business Starter, Pocketwire Business Essentials, Pocketwire Business Growth, Pocketwire Business Pro, Pocketwire Business Premier and Pocketwire Business Enterprise.

| | Starter | Essentials | Growth | Pro | Premier | Enterprise |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| New-seller period (calendar days after the customer's first business profile opened) | 90 | 90 | 60 | 30 | 30 | 30 |
| Completed sales after which the new-seller hold no longer applies | 25 | 25 | 15 | 10 | 5 | 5 |
| New-seller hold (calendar days from the sale date) | 21 | 21 | 14 | 7 | 7 | 7 |
| High-ticket multiple (times the average sale over the previous 30 days) | 5 | 5 | 6 | 8 | 10 | 12 |
| High-risk hold, also used for a sales-limit excess (calendar days from the sale date) | 21 | 21 | 21 | 14 | 10 | 7 |
| Early release after carrier-confirmed delivery (calendar days after the delivery date) | 3 | 3 | 2 | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| Claimed amount held while a buyer claim on the sale is open | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes |

Footnotes to the table:

1. The new-seller period and the completed-sales count are read across every business profile the customer holds, the period running from the customer's first business profile.
2. The early-release figure applies to a new-seller hold or a high-risk hold on the delivered sale; a dispute hold lasts until its claim closes.
3. Example of reading a row (hypothetical sale): on Pocketwire Business Growth, a sale made on the 10th of a month under a new-seller hold is due for release 14 calendar days later, on the 24th.
